articles.title: Gefechte in Aleppo: Was hinter den Gefechten in Nordsyrien steckt
articles.teaser: In Aleppo beschießen sich die kurdisch geführte SDF und Regierungstruppen. Das hat mit einem abgelaufenen Abkommen und einer ungelösten Frage seit Al-Assads Sturz zu tun.
articles.image_title: Gefechte in Aleppo: ALEPPO, SYRIA - JANUARY 6: A soldier from Syrian army forces arriving to the hospital after being wounded on January 6, 2026 in Aleppo, Syria. More than a dozen people have been injured and at least four killed in clashes that broke out between Syrian government forces and the Kurdish-led and US-backed Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) in Aleppo on Tuesday. Heavy shelling was reportedly launched from the SDF-controlled neighborhoods of Sheikh Maqsoud and al-Ashrafia, striking surrounding areas. The escalation in tensions comes amid the stalled implementation of an agreement reached last year to integrate SDF forces into Syrian state institutions under the interim government. (Photo by Adri Salido/Getty Images)

The deadly clashes, which started on January 6, are the worst between the two sides, who have so far failed to implement a March deal to merge the Kurds' semi-autonomous administration and military into Syria's new Islamist government. (Photo by Bakr ALkasem / AFP via Getty Images)
